citation: May, H., Sirinides, P., Gray, A., & Goldsworthy, H. (2016). Reading Recovery: An Evaluation of the Four-Year i3 Scale-Up. Philadelphia, PA: Consortium for Policy Research in Education (CPRE), University of Pennsylvania.
report_number: CPRE Research Report (i3 Scale-Up evaluation); ERIC ED593261
design: RCT; student-level random assignment within schools using matched pairs (the eight lowest-OS-scoring 1st graders per school matched into 4 pairs by ELL status and baseline Text Reading Level, one of each pair randomized to treatment vs delayed-treatment business-as-usual control); 4-year multi-site trial 2011-12 to 2014-15; 1,254 schools randomized students, analytic sample 6,888 students (3,444 matched pairs) in 1,122 schools; subject = Reading; grade 1 (registry grade band K-2). Reading Recovery is a one-to-one literacy intervention delivered by specially trained/PD'd teachers; control = regular classroom literacy instruction plus any non-Reading-Recovery supplemental supports.
problems: The registry codes assignment as Student-level, but impact estimates come from an HLM (PROC MIXED, REML) with school-level random intercepts and slopes plus a matched-pair random effect, so they already account for clustering (cluster_adjusted=true). No single design-effect ICC is reported, so icc is left null (not guessed); n_clusters=1122 schools recorded. The report standardizes two ways: Glass's Delta (impact / control-group SD, a within-sample SD) and Cohen's d (impact / external national-norm SD). I computed Hedges' g using the within-sample CONTROL-group SD (Glass's Delta convention, the standard meta-analytic SMD denominator); using the national-norm SD instead would give the report's smaller Cohen's d (Total 0.37 vs Glass 0.48). The choice of standardizer is the main ambiguity; both sets of numbers are provided in notes. Pretest-posttest correlation was low (ITBS Total r=.31), but the impact estimate is already pretest-adjusted via the HLM (pretest fixed effect beta1). The Observation Survey (OS) outcome is the program's own aligned screening/diagnostic instrument, administered by Reading Recovery teachers (not independent), so it is recorded as researcher_made/secondary and would normally be filtered out centrally.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Reading Recovery (TPD-trained one-to-one literacy intervention) vs business-as-usual
effect_sizes.test_name: Iowa Tests of Basic Skills (ITBS) Total Reading scale score
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (immediately after 12-20 weeks of treatment, ~mid-year of grade 1); pooled across 4 study years 2011-12..2014-15
effect_sizes.g_method: d = impact / control-group SD = 3.41 / 7.16 = 0.4763 (Glass's Delta, matches report's reported Glass D = 0.48). Hedges' g = J*d, J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1) with df = n_t+n_c-2 = 6886, J = 0.99989, g = 0.4762. g_se = J*(impact_se/sd_c) = 0.99989*(0.16/7.16) = 0.02234; g_var = g_se^2 = 0.000499. Impact estimate and SE are the pooled HLM least-squares-means treatment-control difference (Table 2.5 / Appendix Table A13 Pooled column).
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 2.5 (p. 39-40); Appendix Table A13 'Pooled' (p. ~154); Appendix Table A10 HLM params (p. 156); descriptive means Table 2.4 (p. 38)
effect_sizes.notes: Pre-specified primary confirmatory outcome. Pooled impact 3.41 ITBS scale points, p<.0001, 95% CI 3.09-3.72. Report's two standardized effect sizes: Glass's Delta = 0.48 (control SD 7.16, used here); Cohen's d = 0.37 (national-norm SD 9.1). mean_t/sd_t (138.8/7.5) and mean_c/sd_c are descriptive posttest stats from Table 2.4 (control SD 7.16 is the standardizer footnoted in Table 2.5; Table 2.4 lists control SD 7.2). Year-specific Glass deltas ranged 0.42-0.55 (Table A13); year-specific Cohen d's 0.30-0.42. HLM: school random intercept+slope, matched-pair random effect, grouped treatment/control residual variances, pretest fixed effect, year fixed effect + treatment*year interaction; REML in SAS PROC MIXED.

effect_sizes.notes: EXPLORATORY and NOT an independent measure: the OS is Reading Recovery's own screening/diagnostic/monitoring instrument, administered one-to-one by Reading Recovery teachers and aligned to the intervention; the meta-analysis included only independent measures, so this should be filtered out centrally (recorded for completeness). Impact 43.49 points, p<.01. Very large effect (Glass's Delta 0.89; report Cohen's d 0.99 using national-norm SD 43.96), consistent with the outcome being aligned to the treatment. OS analytic sample n=6,644 (treatment 3,371; control 3,322). Pretest-posttest r for OS was high (.60).
